steps.title: Identify the arc

lines.text: $\hl{1}{\angle AOC}$ is the angle at the centre and $\hl{2}{\angle ABC}$ is the angle at the circumference, both standing on the arc $AC$.

steps.ask: Which theorem links the angle at the centre to the angle at the circumference on the same arc? Use it to find ∠ABC.
steps.title: Apply Theorem 19

lines.text: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

steps.ask: B is on the minor arc. Which arc does ∠ABC stand on, and what is the angle at the centre on that arc?
steps.title: Find the reflex angle at the centre

lines.text: $B$ is on the minor arc, so the arc that $\hl{2}{\angle ABC}$ stands on is the major arc $AC$. The angle at the centre on that arc is the reflex angle $\hl{1}{AOC}$.

steps.ask: What is the angle at the circumference in terms of the angle at the centre on the same arc? Use your answer from step 1.

lines.text: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc.

problems.note: The unknown is now ∠OPQ, and Theorem 19 only gives the centre angle POQ, so an isosceles-triangle step using the radii OP and OQ is added to finish. Step 1 uses the same theorem.
